gloss: edge of a cliff; critical moment

definitions.gloss: edge of a cliff; brink of a precipice
definitions.explanation: The physical edge of a cliff or steep drop-off.

definitions.gloss: critical moment; last chance; do-or-die situation
definitions.explanation: A figurative sense meaning a desperate or make-or-break situation where failure seems imminent.

examples.english: I stood at the edge of the cliff.

examples.japanese: {崖|がけ}っぷちから{下|した}を{見|み}ると{足|あし}がすくんだ。
examples.english: When I looked down from the cliff edge, my legs froze.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{崖|がけ}っぷちに{近|ちか}づかないように{柵|さく}が{設|もう}けられた。
examples.english: A fence was set up so that children wouldn't approach the cliff edge.

examples.japanese: チームは{崖|がけ}っぷちに{追|お}い{込|こ}まれた。
examples.english: The team was pushed to the brink.

examples.japanese: {崖|がけ}っぷちの{状況|じょうきょう}で{奇跡|きせき}の{逆転|ぎゃくてん}を{果|は}たした。
examples.english: They pulled off a miraculous comeback in a do-or-die situation.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}は{経営|けいえい}の{崖|がけ}っぷちに{立|た}たされていたが、{新|あたら}しい{投資家|とうしか}のおかげで{持|も}ち{直|なお}した。
examples.english: The company was on the brink of collapse, but recovered thanks to a new investor.

notes:
{崖|がけ}っぷち literally means the edge ({淵|ふち}) of a cliff ({崖|がけ}). The っぷち is a colloquial contraction of ぶち, from {淵|ふち}.

The figurative sense is far more common in everyday use, describing desperate situations where one is about to fail or lose everything.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {崖|がけ}っぷちに{立|た}つ (to stand at the brink)
- {崖|がけ}っぷちに{追|お}い{込|こ}まれる (to be driven to the brink)
- {崖|がけ}っぷちの{状況|じょうきょう} (a do-or-die situation)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {瀬戸際|せとぎわ}: critical moment, turning point — more formal, used in serious contexts like diplomacy or life-and-death matters
- {土壇場|どたんば}: the last moment — emphasizes being at the very end with no more time
